subject: Accounting
title: Short-Term vs. Long-Term Debt
description: A 60-second lesson on Short-Term vs. Long-Term Debt.

hook.text: A company owes $2 million. But when it's due changes everything.

buildup.text: Short-term debt (current liabilities) must be paid within twelve months.

discovery.text: Long-term debt stretches over years—mortgages, bonds, multi-year loans.

twist.text: Companies sometimes reclassify long-term debt as short-term when it nears maturity—a red flag.

climax.text: A healthy balance sheet matches the timing of debt to the assets it finances.

punchline.text: It's not just how much you owe. It's when.

quiz.question: What qualifies as a current liability?

details.summary: Debt on the balance sheet is separated into short-term (due within one year) and long-term (due beyond one year). This topic explains why the maturity structure matters, how refinancing risk works, and what the mix reveals about a company's financial strategy.
details.whyItMatters: A company with heavy short-term debt faces constant refinancing risk—if lenders refuse to renew, the company may face a liquidity crisis even if it's fundamentally profitable.
takeaways: Short-term debt (current portion of long-term debt plus short-term borrowings) is due within 12 months
Long-term debt has maturities beyond one year and typically carries higher but fixed interest rates
Companies that rely heavily on short-term debt are exposed to interest rate changes and refinancing risk

faq.question: What is the difference between short-term and long-term debt?
faq.answer: Short-term debt is due within one year and includes commercial paper, revolving credit lines, and the current portion of long-term loans. Long-term debt has maturities beyond one year and includes bonds, term loans, and mortgages.

faq.question: Why does debt maturity matter for investors?
faq.answer: Heavy short-term debt means the company must constantly refinance—repaying old debt with new borrowing. If credit markets tighten or the company's creditworthiness declines, it may not be able to refinance, creating a liquidity crisis even if the business is profitable.
